rules: 'Uniform-cost search' -> DIJK. 'Bidirectional BFS' -> BIDIR. 'Aastar' (list 5) -> ASTAR. 'Greedy algorithm using a heuristic to prioritize paths closer to the goal' (list 1) -> GREEDY. 'Randomized search to explore paths randomly' (list 0) -> RANDOM. Any 'backtracking ...' item separate from DFS -> X1.

extras.X1: recursive backtracking: in 10/10 lists as an item separate from DFS. A pure version (cells unmarked on the way back) is exponential, so it is treated like the catalogue's 'no' methods.
extras.X2: Floyd-Warshall ('Modified Floyd-Warshall algorithm for dynamic grid pathfinding', list 1): a real all-pairs shortest-path algorithm that can solve the task; O(n^3) over up to 900 cells, so a pure version runs out of time on the large cases ('no' method). Extras are carried through C and E; no F1 requirement was written for them.

other_items_not_carried.Welsh-Powell (lists 0,2,6) / 'Welsh-Park: Welsh-Powell is a graph-colouring algorithm and 'Welsh-Park' does not exist: confabulations, in 5 of 10 lists. Not carried.
other_items_not_carried.flood fill (list 5): 'mark reachable cells and reconstruct the path': nearest to WAVE but no distances are mentioned; as stated it is BFS/DFS. Not counted for WAVE.
other_items_not_carried.implementation details: 'modified DFS with pruning', 'visited set / cycle detection', 'memoization', 'queue or stack', 'dictionary of previous cells', 'priority queue' -> not methods.
